biography.plain_text: Jonathan Kidd Clay, known as Jon Clay, is an American entrepreneur and co-founder of Axle Logistics in Knoxville, Tennessee. A University of Tennessee graduate, he built the privately owned freight brokerage with Drew Johnson. The business arranges road and rail shipments and warehousing for customers across the United States, Canada and Mexico.

long_biography.plain_text:
Freight entrepreneur Jon Clay made reliable payment an early priority at Axle Logistics. With a new brokerage licence and little trading history, the business struggled to win acceptance from factoring companies. Clay and his partner paid half the transport charge upfront, settling the balance after delivery, while working towards profitability.

Clay also favoured keeping sales and operations together so customers had continuity of service. Axle developed specialist staff training, but demanded standards from its customers too. It stopped serving shippers whose poorly managed facilities wasted drivers’ time and made carriers unwilling to accept loads. That resistance could leave customers paying higher prices on the spot market.
